Title: 'Tauke', couriers and compromised officers: Inside prison's contraband trade [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: From tobacco, ganja and syabu to lighters, matches and mobile phones, inmates can get almost anything they want behind bars for the right price.
A former Taiping Prison warden, who wished to be known only as Aziz, 56, said he had seen it all, after being with the Prisons Department for 20 years before opting for early retirement as a sergeant.
He said it was an "open secret" in some prisons that inmates, outside contacts and, in some cases, officers, were willing to compromise their integrity for bribes.
"We don't have anything to do with them unless its for a fee," he told the
New Straits Times
when asked about wardens' involvement.
Aziz said most prison officers were professional, but said a small number of compromised people could weaken the system.
'TAUKE' CONTROL THE TRADE
Aziz said the network was centred around influential inmates known as "
tauke
", who coordinated orders and linked inmates looking for contraband with those who could get them.
"The
tauke
will deal with
orang kerja
.
Orang kerja
will deal with the wardens," he said.
Orang kerja
refers to inmates assigned to work inside the prison. Many are long-serving prisoners familiar with prison routines, work areas and personnel.
"They know the place, they know the routine and they know  where everyone is working," he said.
Aziz said being an
orang kerja
did not automatically mean an inmate was involved in smuggling, but said some exploited their positions to move items between areas or facilitate contact.
He said prohibited items could be concealed on the person, swallowed or moved through other means, depending on the item and security level.
"Some prisoners will conceal items in their rectum  when they go for court cases. These are known as couriers.
"If they manage to smuggle in the items, they would normally receive a portion of the consignment when they deliver it safely.
"This smuggling method is commonly known as 'rocket'," he told the
NST
.
Tobacco, known as "
habuk
" in prison slang, was among the most commonly smuggled items. A quantity about the size of a toothpaste cap could cost between RM100 and RM150.
Inmates also sought drugs, including ganja, heroin and syabu, as well as lighters, lighter flints, matches and other ignition sources.
Those working in officers' canteens or kitchens could get lighters and bring them into prison blocks, where they could sell them to other inmates.
"Anything that is difficult to get inside will have a price. Sales do  not necessarily have to involve cash. Things could even be bought with plates of meals," he said.
PAYMENTS ROUTED THROUGH OUTSIDE CONTACTS
Aziz said payments were often made through family members or trusted contacts outside prison rather than through  cash inside.
An inmate would place an order, after which the
tauke
would provide a bank  or e-wallet account belonging to an associate outside prison. The inmate's family would then deposit the money, which would be withdrawn and distributed among those involved.
[[nid:1537976]]
Aziz claimed some prison officers received about RM3,000 a month for facilitating access or turning a blind eye. He also claimed a prison officer could charge thousands of ringgit to bring in a box of prohibited items concealed among legitimate goods. He said personnel working different shifts could be involved.
"There are three shifts. One shift will be on the
tauke's
side," he said.
He said payments and prices depended on demand, availability, quantity and the risk of detection. Inmates bringing tobacco into prison could receive part of the consignment as payment.
Aziz said drugs, tobacco and mobile phones were among the most  sought after items by inmates. Mobile phones allowed them to contact people outside prison despite being prohibited.
"Someone wants it, someone can get it, and someone has to bring it in," he said.
SECURITY GAPS
Aziz said searches, X-ray machines and other  checks did not always prevent inmates from concealing prohibited items. Those suspected of hiding contraband could be placed in isolation or quarantine for observation and further checks, but not every attempt was successful.
"Some of them will get through, some of them won't."
Singer and composer Muhammad Yasin Sulaiman, who spent time in Sungai Buloh Prison, had recently  said strict security checks had not stopped drugs from circulating inside.
"There are a lot of drugs in prison, even with all the SOPs (standard operating procedures). They strip us and make us do squats to check," he had said on the Sembang Seram podcast.
Yasin said  drugs were compressed, sealed in plastic and swallowed to smuggle them in, while inmates suspected of carrying drugs in their bodies were made to pass motion.
Responding to Yasin's allegations, Prisons Department senior director of prison policy Mohamad Rosidek Musa said while some negative practices could occur, procedures were in place to prevent them.
"The allegation is not true because in the prison context, we focus on rehabilitation programmes and try to address negative practices in prisons.
"Such a thing (as alleged) does not exist. We have SOPs and regulations to curb negative and undesirable practices. We acknowledge that some things may happen, but not as described," Rosidek had said.
Aziz, meanwhile said, security was only as strong as the people enforcing it.
"Even if you have a scanner, if someone wants to cheat the system, they will look for a way," he said.
Aziz said the system was vulnerable when a handful of "bad apples" accepted money. "It's all about the money."
DRONES ADD NEW DIMENSION
Aziz said drones added a new dimension to prison smuggling by allowing prohibited items to be delivered without requiring a person to pass through a controlled entry point.
"In my time, we didn't have to worry about illicit items being dropped from the air," he said.
In November 2024, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said 55 attempts to smuggle drugs into detention centres using drones had been detected and foiled.
Tapah Prison recorded the highest number of attempts, followed by Alor Star Prison. The minister said all 55 attempts had been detected before the drones breached the security perimeter.
The issue resurfaced this year when police arrested two individuals on July 15 following an attempt to smuggle tobacco into Sungai Udang Prison using a drone. NST has been attempting to contact the Prisons Department for comment for more than a week on the latest allegations and is still awaiting a response.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man convicted of attempted murder in shooting of three Palestinian students in Vermont
Article:
WASHINGTON: A man was convicted by a jury of attempted murder in the late 2023 shooting of three Palestinian American students in Vermont, two of whom were wounded and one was left paralysed from the waist down, prosecutors said on Monday.
Jason Eaton was found guilty on three counts of attempted second-degree murder for the shootings of Hisham Awartani, Tahseen Aliahmad and Kinnan Abdalhamid on Nov 25, 2023, in Burlington, Vermont, prosecutor Sarah George, the Chittenden County state's attorney, said in a statement.
The conviction rejected Eaton's insanity defence and he will be sentenced at a later time, George said. A jury trial commenced in the Chittenden Superior Court a week ago and lasted until Monday.
Eaton faces a sentence of up to life without parole, with a presumptive minimum term of 20 years to serve on each count, George said.
The three Palestinian American students, who grew up in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, were walking in Burlington when Eaton approached and shot them, prosecutors and police said.
Awartani was paralysed from the chest down and now lives with paraplegia, his family said. Aliahmad was struck in the chest and Abdalhamid was struck in the glute while running away, according to prosecutors. Aliahmad and Abdalhamid were visiting Awartani's grandmother over a Thanksgiving break from school.
All three were 20 at the time and wore black-and-white Palestinian keffiyeh scarves while conversing in a mix of English and Arabic when the gunman confronted them, prosecutors said. Their families said on Monday justice "has been rendered" and that they feel relief.
Though Eaton pleaded not guilty, he did not dispute being the shooter. His legal team said he should not be found guilty due to insanity, referring to his claims that US and Israeli intelligence ordered him to carry out the shooting through radio and that God asked him to protect Jewish neighbours.
US rights advocates have noted rising anti-Arab, anti-Muslim and anti-Jewish bias since the start of US ally Israel's devastating assault on Gaza following a deadly October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel.
Some fatal incidents that have sparked alarm include a 2023 deadly stabbing of a 6-year-old Palestinian American child in Illinois, whose killer was sentenced to 53 years in prison and died in custody, and a 2026 San Diego mosque shooting that left five dead, including two teenage suspects.

Title: Lockheed wins US Army missile contract worth up to US$1.2 billion
Article:
BENGALURU: Lockheed Martin said on Monday it had secured a contract worth up to US$1.2 billion from the US Army to produce the Increment 2 variant of the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM).
PrSM is the Army's next-generation long-range precision strike weapon, designed to replace the Army Tactical Missile System, or ATACMS.
Lockheed Martin said the award follows a second successful flight test of the missile's Increment 2 variant, which demonstrated its ability to engage moving maritime targets.
The contract comes as Lockheed ramps up production of the Precision Strike Missile amid rising demand for long-range strike weapons.
In March, the defence giant signed a seven-year agreement with the US Department of War to increase annual production capacity to 550 missiles, building on a US$4.94 billion Army contract awarded last year and following the weapon's first combat use during Operation Epic Fury.

Title: Trump praises leftist Mamdani after meeting in New York
Article:
NEW YORK: President Donald Trump heaped praise Monday onto New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani as the pair set aside their political differences to discuss immigration enforcement and a multi-billion-dollar housing project.
Trump, a Republican, heavily criticised Mamdani before he took office in January — calling him "my little communist" and a "total nut job" — but the two men have since struck a surprisingly warm relationship.
"Hopefully, you're going to be a great (mayor). I'll be able to say you're going to be a great one, and you're off to a start," Trump told Mamdani at a news conference.
Their closed-door talks in Manhattan, which lasted around an hour, marked the pair's third public meeting since Mamdani swept the mayoral election last year.
"We appreciate the president's commitment to the city," Mamdani said of Trump, who was visiting his hometown New York ahead of the United Nations General Assembly.
The 34-year-old said he expressed his "very strong opinions about how we can keep New Yorkers safe" when asked about Trump's culling of Temporary Protected Status for thousands of immigrants as part of mass deportation plans.
Mamdani said they also spoke about a 12,000-home building proposal in New York, which the pair previously discussed in February and would require an estimated US$21 billion in federal government funding.
He said he planned to continue cooperating with Trump, despite acknowledging they have "many disagreements."
"We've both spoken about very different approaches, very different beliefs, and I will continue to have conversations with the president, and frankly with anyone who can deliver relief to the people of this city," Mamdani said.
Trump's visit came as top US television networks essentially boycotted coverage of the president in protest at his decision to ban three outlets, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, from the White House.
Mamdani said he had told Trump that all members of the press would be welcome at their joint press conference, held in front of the mayor's official residence.
"That is something that I believe in, is everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique, that we engage," he told reporters.
Trump, meanwhile, brushed off a suggestion that he had issued the media bans to distract the public from criticism of the war in Iran.
"It's interesting because they (the media) said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me, so I wasn't very worried about that," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea says it tests new combat weapon system
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea said it successfully tested a new weapon on Sunday, overseen by leader Kim Jong Un, state media KCNA reported on Tuesday.
Kim said the test, carried out by North Korea's Missile Administration, was a demonstration of "ultra-modern" defence technology and showed clear progress in modernising its armed forces, according to KCNA.
The report did not elaborate on the specific type of weapon.
The South Korean military said on Sunday that North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast.
The test came days after Pyongyang accused the US of driving tensions on the Korean Peninsula through a series of military drills.
On Monday, the foreign ministers of South Korea, Japan and the United States met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York to agree to coordinate closely for peace, stability and denuclearisation on the Korean Peninsula, according to Seoul's foreign ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two pilots die in helicopter crash fighting California wildfire
Article:
NEW MEXICO: Two pilots died when their helicopter crashed on Sunday afternoon while dropping water on a wildfire in California's Yosemite National Park, authorities said on Monday.
Greg King, with contract firm Precision, was one of the pilots who died, according to a statement from the Alaska Division of Forestry and Fire Protection. The second pilot was not named as family members were still being notified, the agency said.
The pilots were carrying out water bucket drops on the Dome Fire when their Super Puma helicopter went down southeast of Ostrander Lake, according to Connie Lau, a spokesperson for the California team managing the response to the fire.
The cause of the crash is under investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board, the agencies said.
The deaths brought to five the number of helicopter pilots killed in crashes in Colorado, Utah and California this year while fighting wildfires.
The United States is experiencing an intense fire season after a historically low winter snowpack, record temperatures and decades of drought in the US West.
At least 18 people have died fighting US wildfires so far in 2026, according to data from the Wildland Fire Lessons Learned federal agency. That is already more than the full-year average of 17 deaths in recent decades, according to National Interagency Fire Center data.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bukit Aman denies police MPV escorted cable theft vehicle in Ampang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Police have denied claims circulating online that a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) escorted a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables in Kampung Tasik Tambahan, Ampang, last Saturday.
Sinar Harian
reported that Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said police had arrested a cable theft suspect in connection with the incident.
He said claims that the police vehicle was involved in a conspiracy with the cable thieves were untrue.
“The claim that the police vehicle was in collusion with them is untrue.
“The MPV acted based on information from the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters operations room, and the team vehicle also activated its beacon lights in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOP) while carrying out its duties,” he said when contacted by
Sinar Harian
yesterday.
Noor Hisam said the actions of the MPV personnel were in response to a public complaint.
He said one suspect had so far been arrested for further action.
Earlier, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from a house near the scene went viral on several social media platforms, including Facebook and Threads.
The footage prompted various reactions from social media users, including claims that the police vehicle had escorted a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables.
Noor Hisam’s clarification came after the footage sparked questions over the police vehicle’s presence at the scene and its actions during the incident.

Title: Orang Asli man killed in suspected tiger attack while searching for rotan in Sungai Siput
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — An Orang Asli man was killed after he was believed to have been attacked by a tiger while searching for rotan in a forest area near Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor in Sungai Siput yesterday.
Sinar Harian
reported that Zamberi Angah, 42, was found dead in a bamboo clump near a logging road, about 200 metres from where the attack was believed to have taken place.
Zamberi was believed to have entered the Korbu Forest Reserve with a friend to search for rotan.
The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) received a report about the incident at about 4.30pm, after which members of its Wildlife Conservation Unit (UKHM) and Sungai Siput Perhilitan personnel rushed to the location, the report said.
A joint search operation began at about 6.30pm involving personnel from the Lintang police station, Civil Defence Force (APM), Civil Volunteer Corps (RELA), as well as about 30 villagers and logging workers.
The Malay daily reported that Zamberi was found at about 6.58pm in a bamboo clump near the logging road.
An inspection at the scene found bite marks on the victim’s neck and signs that parts of his right knee had been eaten up to the waist.
Signs of a struggle, dragging marks, the victim’s blood, tiger paw prints and pieces of his trousers and socks were also found at the scene, according to the report.
The distance between where the attack was believed to have occurred and where Zamberi’s body was found was estimated at about 200 metres.
Lintang assemblyman and Perak Rural Development, Plantation, Agriculture and Food Industry Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Zolkafly Harun also confirmed the incident in a Facebook post yesterday.
He said the incident was deeply distressing and had left a profound impact on the victim’s family and the local community.
“Allahyarham was attacked by a tiger while searching for rotan in the forest with a friend.
“My wife and I also took the time to visit the deceased’s family to convey our condolences and provide a small contribution to help ease the family’s burden,” he was quoted as saying.
He was reported saying that Perhilitan would assist the victim’s family in obtaining the Wildlife Attack Victim Assistance and provide safety advice to residents.
“A tiger trap will be installed in the near future and I hope monitoring and control measures can be carried out immediately to ensure the safety of residents, especially the Orang Asli community who depend on forest resources for their livelihood,” he said.
He also advised the public not to enter the area temporarily, remain vigilant and comply with the authorities’ instructions.

Title: Maritime industry expert seeks Customs dept ruling on RM220m K8 cargoes, calls for industry-wide SOP on petroleum blending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has been urged to issue a clear written position on the Customs treatment of two petroleum cargoes with a combined declared value exceeding RM220 million, as continued uncertainty could affect shipping agents, terminal operators, cargo owners and other participants in Malaysia’s downstream petroleum sector.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said the company was not asking JKDM to decide the matter in its favour, but to state the applicable law, procedure and documentary requirements in writing.
“This has gone beyond a private commercial disagreement. The industry needs to know whether petroleum cargo declared for transhipment under K8 may be blended or commingled in a Public Licensed Warehouse, what approvals are required, and how the declaration and duty treatment must be handled if the product changes,” he said in a statement today.
The matter concerns two Atlanta Crude Oil cargoes totalling 76,954.325 metric tonnes. The first comprised 34,903.062 tonnes carried by MT Marlin Santorini, while the second comprised 42,051.263 tonnes carried by MT Invictus.
Maritime Network said records reviewed by the company showed that the cargoes were declared under the K8 procedure and discharged into shore tanks at Dialog Terminals Langsat in Johor. The company has asked whether the K8 procedure remained appropriate after the reported blending activity and whether any change in the product’s composition, specifications or tariff classification required a different Customs declaration.
Jeyenderan said Maritime Network had pursued clarification through the proper channels since April, including meetings, formal correspondence, a detailed report submitted in late August, a meeting with officers from JKDM’s Downstream Petroleum Unit on Sept 9 and a further written request sent to the department on the same day.
“After months of emails, meetings, reports and formal letters, the continued absence of a written answer is creating avoidable regulatory uncertainty. A matter involving cargo with a declared value of more than RM220 million should not be left to verbal interpretations,” he said.
He said the latest development was a written response from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) dated Sept 17.
Based on MIDA’s stated understanding of the arrangement, the cargo owner or client retained ownership of the crude oil, blending components and resulting Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil (VLSFO), while Dialog undertook the blending at its Tanjung Langsat facility and held the relevant Manufacturing Licence.
MIDA said the client was therefore regarded as a trading company and was not required to apply for a Manufacturing Licence for that activity. Crucially, MIDA advised that confirmation on whether the activity could be carried out in a Public Licensed Warehouse and whether duties applied to the process or export of VLSFO should be obtained directly from JKDM because those matters fell under Customs’ purview.
“MIDA has answered the question within its jurisdiction and has expressly identified Customs as the authority for the remaining issues. The matter cannot continue moving from one agency to another. The competent authority is now clear, and what is needed is a written Customs position,” Jeyenderan said.
He said the requested clarification should state whether K8 remained valid where crude oil declared under tariff heading HS 2709.00 was reportedly blended into VLSFO under HS 2710.19, whether K1 or another declaration was required, and what import duty, sales tax, excise duty, export duty or other tax treatment applied.
If no duty or tax was payable, JKDM should identify the relevant exemption, suspension, licence condition or other legal basis, he said.
Maritime Network also called for an industry-wide written guideline or operational standard covering liquid petroleum cargo handled under K8, including rules on blending or commingling, licensed-warehouse conditions, product identity, sampling, tariff classification, mass-balance records and the reconciliation of inbound cargo against the final outgoing export.
Jeyenderan said written guidance would protect both the authorities and the industry by ensuring that the same rules were understood and applied at every Malaysian port and terminal.
“A verbal explanation may depend on the officer present on that day. A written position creates consistency, accountability and equal opportunity. If this activity is permitted, the rules should be transparent and available to every qualified Malaysian industry player. If it is not permitted, the industry must be told clearly so that companies can comply,” he said.
He stressed that the RM220 million figure represented the combined declared value of the two cargoes and was not being presented as an estimate of lost government revenue.
“We are not alleging an offence and we are not asking Customs to prejudge any party. We are asking the authority responsible for Customs law and procedure to close the regulatory gap with a written answer supported by the applicable legal basis,” he said.
Maritime Network said it was prepared to publish or fairly summarise any substantive clarification received from JKDM and correct any factual point shown to be inaccurate.

Title: Malaysia backs Saudi sovereignty, calls for end to Houthi hostilities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia has condemned in the strongest terms the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and expressed solidarity with the Kingdom.
Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the security and safety of its population, in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law.
“Malaysia also supports all efforts towards de-escalation and an immediate end to the hostilities,” it said in a statement on Monday.
The statement comes amid an escalation in hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, with Saudi authorities saying a ballistic missile fired towards Riyadh on Sept 19 was intercepted and destroyed.
Saudi Gazette reported that the Houthis also attempted to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in Baish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu, but the attacks were thwarted.
Saudi Press Agency reported that on Sept 14, Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif injured 13 civilians and damaged several houses and vehicles, according to the Saudi-led coalition.
The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.
“Malaysia attaches great importance to its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia, and remains fully committed to further strengthening this partnership for mutual interests of both nations,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Education Ministry opens private schools sector to all investors, no more 30pc Bumi rule
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — A minimum of 30 per cent Bumiputera equity ownership is no longer a requirement for private limited companies operating private educational institutions (IPS) under the Ministry of Education (MOE).
The ministry said the decision was reached following discussions with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry.
“This adjustment was made to meet the current needs of the education sector and ensure participation remains open to all parties wishing to contribute to the nation’s educational development,” MOE said in a statement yesterday.
The ministry noted the concerns raised regarding the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for specific IPS owned by private limited companies, as outlined in the IPS Policy Statement Book published in 2006.
It added that it appreciates the contributions of all IPS operators and will continue working with all stakeholders to benefit the education of Malaysian children. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia taps Gulf air links to grow Middle East tourism
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia is strengthening air connectivity and tourism cooperation with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region to boost tourist arrivals from the Middle East.
The effort was highlighted during an official working visit by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture deputy secretary-general (Tourism) Chua Choon Hwa to Dubai from Sept 13 to 17, where he held discussions with airlines, travel agencies and tourism industry players.
According to Tourism Malaysia’s statement today, among the key outcomes were the signing of Memorandums of Understanding between Tourism Malaysia with Emirates and Qatar Airways to strengthen tourism promotion and joint marketing efforts.
Also present was Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim.
During the visit, Chua also met representatives of other airline partners, including Air Arabia, Gulf Air and Etihad Airways, as well as travel agencies and tourism industry players such as Emirates Holidays, Sharaf Travel, Al Rais Travel and Capital Travel.
The engagements also addressed recent changes and the regional situation in the Middle East, which have temporarily affected aviation and tourism activities in the region.
“Air connectivity is fundamental to this effort. By working closely with leading airlines and travel industry partners, we will make Malaysia more accessible to travellers from the UAE, GCC, and the wider Middle Eastern market,” he said.
Additionally, he said Dubai and Abu Dhabi are important international flight hubs, which could also provide greater opportunities for Malaysia to reach markets in Africa and Europe.
According to Tourism Malaysia, Malaysia has welcomed 30,257 visitors from the GCC region from January to June this year, reflecting the market’s potential in family holidays, luxury travel, Muslim-friendly tourism, shopping, wellness, gastronomy, nature and experiential travel.
The initiatives are also in line with the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign, which aims to increase international visitor arrivals, including from the UAE, GCC and wider Middle Eastern markets.
“Tourism Malaysia will continue to leverage partnership and collaborative initiatives with industry alliances to drive sustained growth from the UAE and GCC region,” the statement read. — Bernama

Title: If inflation is falling, why do Malaysians still feel food prices biting hard?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia’s inflation rate is slowing, yet the cost of a meal or a basket of groceries can still feel high for households.
If inflation is falling, why do a plate of nasi lemak, a basket of groceries or a meal at a restaurant still cost more than they did a year or two ago?
When someone says, “It is because of inflation”, what does that actually mean?
Inflation measures how quickly the overall prices of goods and services are rising, rather than whether prices themselves are high or low.
When inflation falls, prices can continue to increase — only at a slower pace.
Take a plate of nasi lemak that costs RM5.
If its price rises to RM5.50 the following year, that is a 10 per cent increase and if it then rises to RM5.61 the year after, the increase is about 2 per cent.
The nasi lemak still costs RM5.61, even though inflation has fallen from 10 per cent to 2 per cent.
What is inflation, how does it affect pricing?
To break it down, inflation is the rate at which the overall prices of goods and services increase over time.
It does not mean every product becomes more expensive by the same amount.
So, when someone says, “It’s inflation,” they are usually referring to a broader rise in prices.
Inflation itself, however, does not explain why a particular item has become more expensive.
For the nasi lemak, we need to look at its ingredients and other costs.
Did ingredients, wages, rent or other operating costs increase?
Those are possible drivers of a price increase, while inflation measures the broader movement across the economy.
If inflation is falling, why do a plate of nasi lemak, a basket of groceries or a meal at a restaurant still cost more than they did a year or two ago? — Picture by Yusof Isa
Prices can still rise
According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), Malaysia’s headline inflation eased from 1.9 per cent in June to 1.8 per cent in July 2026.
The July figures also show why the 1.8 per cent rate should not be interpreted as every item becoming 1.8 per cent more expensive.
For example, DOSM found that 374 of the 573 items in the CPI basket recorded price increases in July, while another 157 items declined, and 42 remained unchanged.
Of the 374 items that increased, 367 recorded increases of 10 per cent or less.
DOSM also reported that annual inflation averaged 1.4 per cent in 2025, down from 1.8 per cent in 2024.
What is getting pricier?
The latest food data shows why it is useful to look beyond the headline figure.
DOSM reported that Food and Beverages inflation increased from 1.4 per cent in June to 1.8 per cent in July 2026, while the group rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month.
Meat prices increased 3.2 per cent year-on-year, with chicken recording a particularly strong increase, from RM10.25 per kg in 2025 to RM10.88 per kg in 2026.
Chicken inflation itself was 6.7 per cent.
As for food away from home, this increased 2.5 per cent, while food at home rose 1.2 per cent.
Other categories recorded smaller increases with fish and other seafood rose 1.1 per cent, fruits and nuts 1.1 per cent, vegetables 1 per cent, and milk and other dairy products and eggs 0.8 per cent.
Cereals and cereal products, as well as oils and fats, each increased 0.2 per cent.
Prices can also fall
Food prices do not always move upwards.
According to DOSM’s annual 2025 data, Food and Beverages inflation was 2.1 per cent, but several food-at-home categories recorded price declines.
Vegetables fell 4.4 per cent, milk and other dairy products and eggs fell 0.9 per cent, while meat and cereals and cereal products each fell 0.3 per cent.
A household buying more chicken or eating out regularly could therefore feel a stronger increase than one buying more vegetables or cereals.
What about our neighbours?
Malaysia’s experience is not unique.
Food prices can remain relatively contained when supply conditions are favourable, although individual items can still rise.
In Indonesia, Bank Indonesia reported that volatile-food inflation eased to 2.52 per cent year-on-year in July 2026, from 5.58 per cent in June.
This is partly due to harvests of chilli varieties and shallots, while also pointing to coordination between the central and regional governments to control food inflation.
Thailand provides another example, whereby its Trade Policy and Strategy Office reported that food and non-alcoholic beverage prices rose 0.98 per cent year-on-year in April 2026.
Prepared food and some fresh vegetables became more expensive, while several fruits and other food items recorded declines.
Harvests, supply, transport costs, global commodity prices and government measures can all affect what consumers pay.
So, what has been happening in Malaysia?
The moderation reflected factors including lower cost pressures and a stronger ringgit, which helped contain the cost of imported goods and inputs.
Bank Negara also pointed to lower global cost pressures and fuel prices as factors that helped keep inflation contained. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Bank Negara also pointed to lower global cost pressures and fuel prices as factors that helped keep inflation contained.
These factors can reduce some of the pressure on businesses and consumers.
However, they do not mean prices have returned to where they were before earlier increases.
Why meals stay expensive
The price of a plate of nasi lemak is not determined only by the cost of rice, coconut milk, anchovies or eggs.
The seller also has to pay for labour, rent, utilities, transportation, packaging and other operating expenses.
So even if the price of one ingredient falls, the final price paid by the customer does not necessarily fall by the same amount.
There can also be a time lag between a change in an input cost and the price consumers see.
Food prices are also influenced by costs beyond the stall or supermarket such as global commodity prices and movements in the ringgit, which can affect domestic costs.
What does it mean for households?
For households, falling inflation means prices are rising more slowly — it does not mean the nasi lemak has returned to RM5.
The price of a plate of nasi lemak cannot be reversed. — Picture by Soo Wern Jun
Falling inflation is not the same as falling prices, and it also does not erase previous price increases.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) reported that between 2019 and 2024, Malaysia’s headline CPI increased 9.3 per cent, while nominal wages per worker increased by 7.2 per cent.
This does not mean every household experienced those exact changes, instead, it illustrates why households can continue to feel pressure even when the latest inflation rate is relatively low.
A period of lower inflation means prices are not rising as quickly.
So, when the headline inflation rate falls, the question is not simply whether prices are going down, it is also which are rising, which are falling, and whether household incomes are keeping pace.
That is why Malaysians hear inflation is falling yet still feel that their groceries, takeaway meals or favourite nasi lemak are expensive.

Title: ‘This is where we were born’: 9,000 Kampung Bahagia residents wait to rebuild five months after devastating fire
Article:
SANDAKAN, Sept 22 — Where a thousand wooden stilt houses once rose above the water, only blackened ruins remain. The floating village of Kampung Bahagia here was destroyed by a massive fire on April 19, leaving nearly 9,000 residents with nothing but the clothes on their backs.
Against a backdrop of the charred remnants, rows of tents with white canopies — donated by non-governmental organisations — and huts made of plywood line the roadside.
Behind the flimsy walls of those temporary dwellings, some 300 families are struggling to rebuild their lives while awaiting the completion of new housing in the area that had been their “paradise” before the tragedy occurred.
“I now live in a small tent with my seven family members, including three grandchildren. Life without a home is miserable, especially when we have to endure the heat and rain.
“At night, I cannot sleep peacefully because I worry about rain and strong winds. Whenever it rains, we all get wet, and so do our clothes and belongings,” 53-year-old Rohaida Absara told Bernama.
Fire victim Rohaida Absara, 53, repairs her tent after it was torn by strong winds during a recent check on the temporary settlement. — Bernama pic
Glimmer of hope
Rohaida’s family is among the 100 or so families who have been living in the tents since the tragedy, without electricity or a regular supply of clean water.
Whenever dark clouds gather overhead, her anxiety intensifies as she fears the tents could be blown away by strong winds, particularly at night. The families also have to endure scorching daytime heat, as well as the threat of wildlife.
“I never imagined that the house where my family and I had lived for decades would be engulfed by flames and destroyed in the blink of an eye,” she said, her voice filled with sadness.
Simang Damli, 31, who stays in a tent with three other families, said the overcrowded and uncomfortable conditions forced her to send five of her children to stay with relatives, while she remains in the tent with her one-month-old baby.
“Whenever it rains, I take my child to the mosque for shelter as I worry that the canopy will be blown away by the strong wind,” she said.
Simang Damli, 31, shelters in an overcrowded tent with three other families in Sandakan, keeping only her one-month-old baby with her after sending five children to stay with relatives. — Bernama pic
For now, those living in the temporary dwellings depend on water from a nearby hill as well as supplies delivered by water tankers operated by the Sabah Water Department. For electricity, they rely on power sources at the nearby mosque for basic needs such as charging their phones.
Despite the hardships, there is a glimmer of hope for the Kampung Bahagia residents. Bernama was informed that efforts are underway to enable them to rebuild their homes in the village.
Through efforts initiated by the recently formed Kampung Bahagia Village Development and Security Committee (JKKK), the Sabah state government, through the Sabah Lands and Surveys Department (JTU), is actively carrying out site surveying work.
“JTU is currently in the preliminary stage of preparing the site and mapping out the new settlement to facilitate the construction of houses,” said Kampung Bahagia village head Sharif Hashim Sharif Titing.
A view of stilt houses destroyed in a fire at Kampung Bahagia in Sandakan April 19, 2026. — Bernama pic
He said the majority of victims, who are Malaysian citizens, have made their wishes clear: they want to remain in Kampung Bahagia rather than be relocated elsewhere.
For the villagers, the settlement built over the water holds deep sentimental value as their ancestral home and the birthplace of generations of the community.
“The residents very much hope that the community separated by the fire can be reunited on the same site. This is where we were born and where all our memories are kept,” Sharif Hashim said.
He said this is also why residents were willing to stay in temporary structures in nearby areas despite having to live in difficult conditions.
“So far, about 50 tents have been set up by various NGOs, while around 200 small huts have been built by the fire victims themselves on privately owned land with permission (from the owner who has allowed them to reside there temporarily), including my own hut,” he said.
Kampung Bahagia JKKK chairman Mohd Anuar Noah said the committee was formed to monitor the welfare and safety of fire victims sheltering in tents, with personnel conducting night patrols. — Bernama pic
Community spirit
Despite the many shortcomings at the temporary settlement, the spirit of solidarity among Kampung Bahagia residents has remained strong through the establishment of the JKKK.
Its chairman Mohd Anuar Noah said the committee was formed specifically to monitor the welfare and safety of victims sheltering in the tents.
“The residents are exposed to various safety risks, particularly disturbances by animals such as stray dogs that frequently roam the area at night.
“That is why we have personnel conducting night patrols to ensure the tent area remains safe. Thankfully, there have been no untoward incidents so far,” he said.
In terms of health and sanitation, close cooperation among elected representatives, government agencies and NGOs has played an important role in preventing disease outbreaks.
Member of Parliament for Batu Sapi Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan allocated emergency funds for the construction of basic toilets at the site, while Mercy Malaysia is also planning to add two more sanitation units for bathing and washing clothes.
Kampung Bahagia village head Sharif Hashim Sharif Titing said residents want to rebuild on the same site rather than be relocated. — Bernama pic
Solid waste management is carried out regularly by the Sandakan Municipal Council to ensure rubbish is collected on schedule, complemented by residents’ own efforts to organise frequent communal clean-up activities.
Meanwhile, difficulties in obtaining clean water have been eased through water tanker deliveries by the state Water Department at least once every two days, following an official request by the Batu Sapi parliamentary constituency, while residents also share gravity-fed water from a nearby hill.
The concern shown by the country’s top leadership, through Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit with Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor shortly after the tragedy, also provided an early morale boost to the residents.
Financial assistance of RM1,500 for each affected family, RM300 in aid for schoolchildren, as well as free replacement of identification documents have helped ease some of the financial burden borne by the victims.
However, the swift rebuilding of their permanent homes will be the most meaningful step towards healing the wounds of Kampung Bahagia’s 9,000 residents. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s ‘elephant whisperer’ leads push to save Sabah’s endangered Bornean elephants
Article:
SUKAU, Sept 21 — Deep in Malaysia’s Borneo jungle, wild shouts fill the air as a Bornean elephant is darted and her angry herd rallies to protect her.
The downed elephant is one of only around 1,000 Bornean elephants left in the wild, and the team that darted her is working to protect the endangered species by minimising growing conflict between the animals and local communities.
Once the herd has been chased off, conservationist Farina Othman and her team move in to attach a tracking collar to the animal.
This photo taken on August 24, 2026, shows Farina measuring the length of a female Bornean elephant’s leg during a GPS collaring operation as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
The collar allows them to alert villagers if the elephant strays too near.
It is also key to a programme Farina is designing to create “corridors” for elephants roaming a fragmented landscape of virgin forest patches, hemmed in by vast oil palm plantations and villages.
Farina has studied these elephants for years, earning her the nickname “Borneo’s elephant whisperer” as well as the prestigious Whitley Award for conservationists.
This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a wild female Bornean elephant with a GPS collar around her neck crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
“It’s Pigtail,” she whispered, stroking the tranquilised elephant’s trunk and nodding to the distinctive tail that prompted its nickname.
The team works fast — the dart’s sedative effects last only half an hour, and the herd can still be heard nearby. Overhead, there are flashes of lightning as a tropical thunderstorm approaches.
As soon as the collar is securely fastened and blood samples are taken, the team, accompanied by AFP journalists, retreat into the forest before Pigtail rouses.
‘Conflict inevitable’
This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a herd of wild Bornean elephants crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
For the past 40 years, Bornean elephants have lost more than 60 per cent of their habitat in Sabah, in northern Borneo, to logging and, later, oil palm expansion, according to the International Union for Conservation of Nature, which listed the animal as endangered in 2024.
Lower Kinabatangan, a floodplain in eastern Sabah of around 400 square kilometres, is home to around 160 elephants.
But “only half of that is now a space left for the elephants,” said Farina, a Malaysian academic who heads local conservation group Seratu Aatai, or “Solidarity” in the local Sungai language.
When the animals venture into private property or nearby villages, “conflict is inevitable”, she told AFP.
This aerial photo taken on August 26, 2026, shows a general view with the Kinabatangan River and surrounding jungle in Sukau, a small village near Sandakan in Sabah state on the island of Borneo. — AFP pic
In a recent incident, a herd of 20 elephants stomped into palm oil smallholdings and three villages, terrifying residents.
No one was injured, but the incident prompted calls for stronger deterrents, including upgraded electric fencing.
“People don’t feel safe around elephants, and that’s when conflict happens,” Farina said.
The animosity worsens when the animals, especially adventurous bulls, which can weigh up to five tonnes, cleverly bypass electric fencing to feast on palm trees or saplings.
That is why Farina and her team of 17 conservationists prioritise coexistence.
A herd of wild Bornean elephants crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
“We’re working to increase people’s tolerance, to increase connectivity space for elephants and to find a long-term solution,” she said.
Based in Sukau, a hamlet on the crocodile-infested banks of the Kinabatangan river, Seratu Aatai runs an outreach programme in plantation schools, distributes information pamphlets and has designated “community wildlife guardians” who help usher away elephants that have wandered into human habitation.
“Before, we didn’t know how to manage living near them,” said homestay owner Firah Kazenn, 21, who recently encountered elephants behind her home in Sukau.
“The elephants were unmonitored, and many were lost to conflict. Now, with the Seratu Aatai unit, they are protected, and the community is actively involved too,” Firah told AFP.
This photo taken on August 27, 2026, shows boats docked along the shore of the Kinabatangan River and surrounded with jungle in Sukau. — AFP pic
“We’ve learnt safe ways to guide the elephants away when they come too close to our homes, without harming them,” she added.
‘Win-win situation’
Farina believes the best way to protect the animals is by creating “elephant corridors” — pathways through plantations connecting patches of habitat.
She is hoping to convince seven plantations in the area that elephants are “an ecological reality, rather than an occasional disturbance”.
But it will be a challenge.
Fierce competition driven by tight, volatile margins means many producers are not keen to sacrifice land for corridors, said Muhammad Al Shafieq bin Mustafa, a former plantation manager in Sukau and now a palm oil industry specialist.
Members of the team led by Farina measuring the length of a female Bornean elephant during a GPS collaring operation as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
“Those plantations that do commit and are willing to work with people like Farina often do not get the recognition that they deserve or the financial support that they need, especially from Western palm oil buyers,” he told AFP.
Industry-funded conservation associations say plantations have made progress in becoming sustainable palm oil producers but face difficult economic realities.
“It needs to be a win-win situation between the planters and also the wildlife,” said Daniel Pamin, conservation and sustainability executive at the Malaysian Palm Oil Green Conservation Foundation.
This photo taken on August 24, 2026, shows Nabila Sarkawi, a veterinary officer with the Sabah Wildlife Department at Sepilok (back), watching Khairun Amlan (right) administering a multivitamin injection during a GPS collaring operation led by Farina (unseen) as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
Farina believes change will come.
Before, locals used the Malay word “halau”, meaning “chase away” or “banish”, when talking about elephants.
“Now, we are working to get people to say... ‘walking’ or ‘escorting’ out the elephant.” — AFP
A wild male Bornean elephant crossing the Kinabatangan River with a plastic bag wrapped around its trunk in Sukau. — AFP pic

Title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks, stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Malaysia has condemned in the strongest terms the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and expressed solidarity with the Kingdom.
Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the security and safety of its population, in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law.
“Malaysia also supports all efforts towards de-escalation and an immediate end to the hostilities,” it said in a statement on Monday.
The statement comes amid an escalation in hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, with Saudi authorities saying a ballistic missile fired towards Riyadh on September 19 was intercepted and destroyed.
Saudi Gazette
reported that the Houthis also attempted to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in Baish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu, but the attacks were thwarted.
Saudi Press Agency reported that on September 14, Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif injured 13 civilians and damaged several houses and vehicles, according to the Saudi-led coalition.
The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.
“Malaysia attaches great importance to its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia, and remains fully committed to further strengthening this partnership for mutual interests of both nations,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Five-year-old girl found dead after uncle allegedly throws her into river in Johor
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 21 — A five-year-old girl was found dead, believed to have been thrown into a river by her uncle in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, this morning.
Kota Tinggi District Police Chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9:30am regarding a 37-year-old local man who went on a rampage armed with a machete while chasing a 40-year-old man.
He said initial investigations found that prior to the incident, the suspect was believed to have thrown the victim into the river.
“Acting on information, a police team went to the location of the incident, and a struggle ensued resulting in injuries to one of the personnel, but the suspect was eventually arrested,” he said in a statement today.
Yusof said a medical assistant confirmed the death, and the victim’s body was sent to Kota Tinggi Hospital before being brought to the Forensic Department of Pasir Gudang Hospital tomorrow for a post-mortem.
He added that the motive and cause of the incident are still under investigation, and the suspect is also believed to have mental health issues.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Anwar leaves Istana Negeri Sembilan after hour-long audience with Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held a nearly hour-long audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, this evening, as a dispute over the status of the state executive council continued to unfold.
Anwar left Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here after completing the audience, Astro Awani reported.
He had arrived at the palace grounds at about 6pm.
No details of the discussions during the meeting were immediately disclosed.
The audience came after Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members with immediate effect late last night.
According to a statement by Istana Negeri Sembilan comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali, the decision was made after the ruler found that the exco members had breached their oaths of office.
The palace cited Article 38(5) of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959, which states that a member of the State Executive Council holds office for as long as he or she has the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The exco members had taken their oaths and signed pledges of loyalty on August 7 before being appointed to the council.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, however, disputed the validity of their removal in a statement today.
He said any action to dismiss or terminate the membership of an exco member without the advice or formal request of the Menteri Besar was “invalid, unconstitutional and had no legal effect”.
Ismail said he had not been consulted or provided advice on the removal of any exco member under Article 38(5).
He maintained there was therefore no need to submit a new list of proposed exco members, saying the existing line-up remained legally valid and would continue to carry out its duties as usual.

Title: MOH moves on compensation for Sarawak helicopter crash victims’ families, flying doctor service stays grounded
Article:
TAIPING, Sept 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is collaborating with the Public Service Department’s (PSD) Pension Division and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to ensure a smooth process for granting death ex-gratia payments, retirement benefit claims, and other benefits to the families and heirs of the victims who perished in the flying doctor service (FDS) operation helicopter crash in Sarawak on September 8.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measure is currently underway to ensure that the surviving next of kin receive appropriate justice and support.
“I cannot state the details, but the calculations include everything in great detail, and they are currently computing all of that. The ex-gratia has many components to it,” he told reporters after conducting a working visit to the Taiping Hospital here today.
The crash on September 8 claimed the lives of all five individuals on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3:40pm.
The victims who perished were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31, two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44, as well as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30.
Meanwhile, he said the MOH has not set a specific timeframe for the suspension of FDS operations in Sarawak following the temporary suspension, adding that operations will only resume after the authorities complete their official investigation findings.
“As soon as we can restart, we will restart. We won’t wait. But until a decision is made, everything depends on the investigation results and so forth. So, we will wait to get the investigation results, and immediately after that, we will take steps to make decisions regarding subsequent services,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the MOH has allocated over RM1.65 million to upgrade and improve facilities at Taiping Hospital adding that the allocation involves upgrading, renovation, and repair works covering healthcare facilities, restrooms, and other areas.
According to him, this amount is an increase compared to the allocation of RM571,000 last year for improvement works involving the hospital’s Emergency Department and psychiatric ward, which has already been fully completed. — Bernama

Title: Anwar arrives at Istana Negeri Sembilan for audience with Tuanku Muhriz amid state exco shake-up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — A convoy believed to be carrying Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived at Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here at about 6pm today.
Anwar is expected to have an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, following developments over the status of the state executive council (exco).
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim are also expected to have an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.
Members of the media began gathering outside the palace at about 3pm to follow developments.
In a statement last night, Comptroller of the Royal Household of Istana Negeri Sembilan Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali announced that Tuanku Muhriz had revoked the appointments of the state executive councillors with immediate effect.
The palace said the decision was made after Tuanku Muhriz found that the exco members had breached their oaths of office.
Azizi said that under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959, an eexco member, other than the Menteri Besar, holds office at the pleasure of the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
The exco members had taken their oaths and signed pledges of allegiance on Aug 7 before being appointed to the council.
Following the revocation, the menteri besar is required to submit a new list of exco candidates for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration and consent under Article XXXVIII(2) of the state constitution. — Bernama

Title: Najib’s residence assessed for house arrest, but location not yet finalised, authorities say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Police and the Prisons Department held a coordination meeting today to assess the security aspects of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence in preparation for the former prime minister’s house arrest.
Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the meeting between the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Prisons Department took place at Najib’s residence here, however, clarified that the location for the house arrest has not yet been finalised as the authorities have not yet received the official order document.
“It has not been finalised because we have not yet received the order. It will be finalised once the order is obtained, and there will be specific conditions attached,” he told reporters outside Najib’s residence here today.
Elaborating on the meeting details, Anuar Bakri who was seen arriving at the residence around 2:30pm, explained that the police were present to examine security aspects outside the residential area, while the Prisons Department oversaw matters related to the detention itself.
Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said police are assessing security outside Najib Razak’s residence while the Prisons Department handles detention arrangements. — Bernama pic
“There are no specific details yet, one of the matters discussed was an assessment of Najib’s residence. The Prisons Department requested the police to join them to look at the situation from our perspective — specifically regarding security,” he said.
Regarding security control procedures in the area, Anuar Bakri denied claims that additional structures, such as barbed wire or special iron fencing, would be installed at the residence.
Last Friday, His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia granted a conditional pardon to Najib, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department announced that the decision was reached during the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya, held at Istana Negara.
The former Member of Parliament for Pekan has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million in funds belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd. — Bernama

Title: Former High Court judge Duncan Sikodol joins MACC Advisory Board
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Former High Court judge Datuk Duncan Sikodol has been appointed to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) Anti-Corruption Advisory Board for the 2026-2029 term.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he presented Duncan with his instrument of appointment today.
“May the trust placed in him further strengthen efforts to combat corruption while enhancing the country’s integrity and governance,” Anwar posted on Facebook. — Bernama

Title: Cops confirm arson at two 24-hour convenience stores in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 21 — Two 24-hour convenience stores here were targeted by unknown persons in separate arson attacks on Sunday night.
Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the incidents occurred between 7.05pm and 8.30pm.
“The first incident, which occurred in the King Centre area, involved the use of firecrackers and did not result in any losses.
“In the second incident along Jalan Green, two male suspects came to the premises and threw an object inside, causing two explosions and a fire,” he said in a statement on Monday.
The fire was extinguished by Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) personnel.
Alexson said police are investigating both incidents under Section 436 of the Penal Code, for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy.
Conviction carries up to 20 years’ imprisonment and possible fine.
“PDRM Sarawak is actively conducting investigations to track down and arrest the suspects, analyse the materials used, examine closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and determine whether there is any link between the two incidents.
“The motive is still under investigation, and the cases are being investigated under Section 436 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy a house or building,” he said in a statement on Monday.
He said preliminary investigations found that the two suspects had a similar modus operandi, with both masked and dressed in dark clothing before entering the premises and throwing objects believed to contain explosive or flammable materials into the stores.
Mohamad Zainal said police would also investigate claims circulating that the convenience stores were selling online gambling ‘top-ups’ and take appropriate action, including applying to the local authorities to revoke their business licences.
“The public is advised against making speculation that could jeopardise the investigation.
“Owners of business premises are advised to enhance security measures and immediately report to the police if they detect any suspicious individuals or vehicles,” he stressed.
He said efforts are ongoing to trace and identify those behind the attacks.
“Members of the public with information on the incidents are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Tan Chiang Fook on 018-2628805 or the Kuching district police headquarters operations room on 082-244444,” he said.
Meanwhile, Bomba in a separate statement said a call on the fire at the Jalan Green convenience store was received at 8.19pm.
It said the fire damaged 35 per cent of the store, starting at the front and spreading towards the centre of the shop.
“No injuries were reported in the incident. Personnel from the Batu Lintang and Padungan fire stations wrapped up the operation at 9.03pm after ensuring there was no risk of the fire reigniting,” the department said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Man found dead in petrol station toilet near Tronoh
Article:
IPOH, Sept 21 — A 39-year-old local man was found dead inside the toilet of a petrol station in Taman Tronoh Baru, near Tronoh, today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said they received an emergency call at 2:20pm before a team of personnel from the Batu Gajah Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene at 2:34pm.
“Upon arrival, the police and the Ministry of Health (MOH) were already at the scene and found a man lying unconscious, as well as stuck in the toilet door frame.
“The victim was later confirmed dead by the MOH, and it was informed that the victim was a member of the public who had stopped by to use the toilet at the petrol station,” he said in a statement today.
He said firemen then carried out operations to extricate the victim, who was stuck in the door frame, by adjusting the victim’s position until he was successfully removed from the toilet.
He added that the victim’s body was brought out and handed over to the police for further action before the operation fully concluded at 3pm. — Bernama

Title: ‘Urgent and important’: Serikin border complex fast-tracked for 2027 completion, says minister
Article:
BAU, Sept 21 — Construction of the RM43.66 million Serikin Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex has recorded 11.23 per cent physical progress as of yesterday and is expected to be completed by the end of next year.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the border security project under the National Security Council (MKN) was placed in the ‘urgent and important’ category for fast-track implementation.
“This project is also among the matters discussed in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Meeting as well as the MA63 Technical Committee Council.
“This is important. It is among the government’s efforts to ensure border projects can be upgraded so that we can safeguard the country’s sovereignty, especially in Sabah and Sarawak,” he told reporters after conducting a working visit to the project site here today.
The construction project includes the main building and inspection counters, four units of quarters, a surau, a canteen, a guardhouse, as well as mechanical and electrical services.
Commenting on the challenges of the project, Mustapha said logistics, road construction and the provision of electricity, water and telecommunications services needed to be given special attention to avoid operational delays once the building was completed.
Meanwhile, Mustapha, who also visited the border control post (PKS) project site in Telok Melano-Temajuk, said the project was in the final phase of the tender process for the appointment of a contractor before the issuance of the Letter of Acceptance (SST).
He said the PKS was expected to be completed in another two years.
“Do not consider projects involving national security as ordinary projects. This is actually what needs to be understood by all agencies, departments, ministries, contractors and other parties involved in this project,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh: Loke’s resignation offer was DAP CEC’s final decision, must be respected
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister was the final decision of the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) and must be respected.
DAP CEC deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh said the CEC meeting last Saturday also heard various proposals and views before the decision was made.
“The CEC held a lengthy meeting, and various proposals and views were put forward. The final decision, the CEC’s decision; this is the highest decision-making body, was that YB Anthony Loke offered to resign.
“That was the CEC’s decision. I do not want to disclose the other discussions as they were part of the CEC deliberations, but we have to respect the decision made by the CEC,” she said at a press conference on the 2026 Deepavali Bazaar here today.
Hannah said this in response to the DAP CEC’s decision following its meeting on the party’s stance on the issue of a conditional pardon for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Last Saturday, Loke offered to resign as Transport Minister following DAP’s stance on the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
Loke said the resignation would only involve him as a member of the Cabinet, while the other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the government to ensure continued political stability in the country. — Bernama

Title: Beyond trade: Anwar’s fourth China visit targets AI, digital economy and skills
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou beginning Tuesday is aimed at deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting the importance of technical talent development.
In his three-day working visit on the invitation of the Chinese government, Anwar’s robust itinerary centres on a high-level bilateral meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, alongside engagements at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 and the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou.
“This is the prime minister’s fourth visit to China (since becoming prime minister in 2022). This shows how familiar and close the relationship between Malaysia and China is.”
“Although this is a working visit, the prime minister has been honoured by Premier Li Qiang with a bilateral meeting between Malaysia and China, and also a dinner to be held in Hangzhou,” Malaysia’s Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad told the Malaysian media ahead of the prime minister’s arrival here on Tuesday.
He said Anwar’s visit also aimed at initiating cooperation in new fields outside of traditional fields, such as education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), digital economy and AI.
The prime minister will also deliver a keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 and at the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, will be accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The prime minister is scheduled to hold talks with Li in Hangzhou, providing both leaders with another opportunity to review bilateral projects and explore strategic cooperation of the countries.
Norman said that during the meeting, the two leaders are expected to discuss several matters to strengthen bilateral relations under the framework of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, in line with the aspiration of building a High-Level Strategic Malaysia–China Community with a Shared Future and President Xi Jinping’s initiatives including the Global Development Initiative (GDI) and the Global Civilisation Initiative (GCI).
Norman said the bilateral meeting was also expected to discuss the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) extension project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang which will benefit connectivity and economic development.
Also discussed was the implementation of the upgrading of the Two Countries, Twin Parks project following the signing of a memorandum of understanding on April 17, 2025.
Apart from that, it also touched on the prime minister’s visit to Shenzhen in conjunction with the Apec Leaders’ Summit to be held in November this year as well as Malaysia’s participation as a founding member country of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation (WAICO).
While in Hangzhou, Anwar is also scheduled to launch a book titled
Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform and Ignorance in Postnormal Times
which has been translated into Chinese.
Norman said China had remained Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) for the period of January to August.
Anwar is also slated to meet Chinese captains of industry as part of efforts to attract quality investments into Malaysia.
The session is expected to showcase investment opportunities in data centres, AI, semiconductors, electric vehicles, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing, logistics and the digital economy. — Bernama

Title: KL mayor: Sunday flash floods hit city after Ampang, Lembah Keramat record 155mm rainfall
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas.
Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital.
“Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.
“As of 5.30pm, Lembah Keramat recorded the highest accumulated rainfall at 155.5 mm, compared with the usual 30 mm,” he said during a press conference here today.
According to media reports, heavy rain that swept across the federal capital on Sunday afternoon resulted in flooding in several areas, including Ampang, Taman U-Thant and Jalan Ampang, disrupting traffic.
On the issue of foreign worker accommodation at the Federal Territory Affordable Housing Project (Residensi Max) on Jalan Kolam Air, Fadlun said the Commissioner of Buildings (COB) had warned the project developer against converting utility rooms into accommodation for foreign workers.
“Residensi Max remains under the developer’s supervision. Therefore, the COB has issued a warning letter to the developer, reminding the developer not to house workers in areas or rooms designated for other purposes, and we will continue to monitor the situation,” he said.
The media had previously reported concerns among Residensi Max residents over the presence of foreign nationals at the residence, with the situation allegedly having persisted for nearly a year.
Residensi Max Residents’ Association chairman Muhammed Assyafiq Ahmad Kamal reportedly expressed frustration with the management, alleging that it had refused to cooperate with residents to resolve the issue. — Bernama

Title: Selangor expands Kita Selangor Voucher eligibility, households earning RM8,000 or below now qualify
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — The Selangor government has expanded the eligibility threshold for the Kita Selangor Voucher (BKS) to include households with a monthly income of RM8,000 or below.
State Women’s Development and Social Welfare Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said the phased rollout of the programme was introduced under the Selangor Resilience Strengthening Package to assist citizens affected by the rising cost of living and economic uncertainty resulting from global supply crises.
It initially prioritised vulnerable groups such as single mothers and heads of hardcore-poor households before extending eligibility to households earning RM5,000 or less.
“The state government has further expanded the eligibility threshold to include households earning RM8,000 or less. Applications must be submitted via the SELangkah app,” she said in a statement today.
She said applicants who are currently under review, were previously rejected, or are appealing will have their cases reassessed under the revised criteria,” she said.
The key requirements include Malaysian citizen and a registered voter residing in Selangor.
“Married couples or single parents must have at least one child aged 18 or younger and a household income of RM8,000 or less.
“Only one recipient is allowed per household, and the applicant must not be an active recipient of the Selangor Prosperous Living Aid (BINGKAS) programme,” she said.
For further information regarding eligibility criteria, the application process, and implementation, please visit the official BKS portal at https://baucarkitaselangor.com/. — Bernama

Title: JPJ nets RM91.2m from ‘H’ series plates, confirms RM10.7m winning bid for ‘H 1’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — The Road Transport Department, better known by its Malay initials JPJ, collected RM91.2 million from bidding for the new “H” series special registration numbers (NPI), with a single plate, H 1, fetching RM10,777,777, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) said today.
In a media statement, the ministry said the total of RM91,206,642 came from bidding held entirely on the JPJeBid system from Sept 16 to 20.
Of that, RM89,266,542 was bid revenue and RM1,940,100 was service fees. The series was introduced to mark Malaysia Day 2026.
A total of 34,664 bidders took part, and 8,223 registration numbers were successfully bid on. That works out to an average of roughly RM10,860 per number sold, based on the bid revenue.
H 1 was the highest bid by a wide margin. The next highest was H 9 at RM4,969,999, followed by H 3 at RM4,209,777, H 5 at RM4,007,777 and H 8 at RM4 million. H 6 went for RM3.38 million, H 2 for RM3.18 million and H 7 for RM3.1 million. H 4 fetched RM2,437,777 and H 11 RM1,557,777.
The numbers that drew the most bidders were H 1001 and H 100, with 37 each. They were followed by H 1805 with 36 bidders, and H 1777 and H 4818 with 32 each.
The ministry called the result proof of the success of the government’s digital transformation through JPJeBid, which it said makes bidding easier, faster, more efficient and more transparent.
It said all proceeds will go back to the public through MOT and JPJ programmes, including road safety and initiatives that benefit the community directly.

Title: Putrajaya condemns Al-Aqsa storming, warns provocations risk sparking wider global conflict
Article:
